title: CBP seizes $290,680 in cocaine at Laredo's Juárez-Lincoln Bridge
excerpt: CBP officers found 20 packages with 49.3 pounds of alleged cocaine hidden in a car referred for secondary inspection at the Juárez-Lincoln Bridge on October 23, Texas Border Business reported October 28.
content:
U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers seized 49.3 pounds of alleged cocaine, valued at an estimated $290,680, at the Laredo Port of Entry, according to Texas Border Business, which reported the CBP account on October 28.

The seizure happened Friday, October 23, at the Juárez-Lincoln Bridge, when an officer referred a 2019 Honda Accord for a secondary inspection. A nonintrusive inspection then revealed 20 packages containing the alleged cocaine hidden inside the vehicle, according to the report.

The vehicle was driven by a 36-year-old U.S. citizen, with a 17-year-old passenger, the report said. CBP seized the narcotics and the vehicle, arrested the driver, and Homeland Security Investigations special agents are investigating the seizure.

Port Director Albert Flores said in a statement quoted in the report: “Officers at the Laredo Port of Entry consistently demonstrate vigilance in protecting our nation from dangerous narcotics. Their dedication to safeguarding our communities remains second to none.”

What to watch next: whether investigators announce charges or further details as the Homeland Security Investigations inquiry continues.

Sources:

  • Texas Border Business, “CBP Officers Seize over $290K in Cocaine at Laredo Port of Entry,” October 28, 2026
